architecture.title: A coding agent on local inference — the agent edits files, the Spark's model only returns tool calls
architecture.caption: The playbooks run the agent on the Spark next to Ollama (ollama launch <agent>). To run it on your laptop, reach the Spark's Ollama through an ssh tunnel (course default) or by opening port 11434 (vibe-coding Step 2, no authentication). Each client speaks a different Ollama API: native /api for ollama launch and Continue, /v1/chat/completions for OpenCode, /v1/messages for Claude Code, /v1/responses for Codex. Lab 01 checks all four.

sequence.title: Lab 18-2 — one edit, graded by the real test
sequence.caption: The model never touches the disk: it returns a write_file tool call. The lab (acting as the agent) checks the call, writes the file into a temp dir, runs the test, and on failure gives the model the test output for one repair turn. A reply with no tool call, or a tool call printed as text, is a failed edit.

steps.label: valid JSON? right path? screen os/subprocess/open
write file · run test_* (20 s timeout)
on FAIL: tool result = test output, 'fix it'
scorecard: tool call · valid args · pass 1st · pass ≤1 repair

charts.title: Lab 18-2 on this Mac — edits that passed their tests, 3 runs × 3 tasks
charts.caption: LAPTOP STAND-IN, measured: three runs of lab 02 on this Mac's Ollama 0.34.4, one trial per task each. Model behaviour, not speed. nemotron-3-nano printed its parse_duration tool call as text in all three runs; gemma3:4b has no tools capability. Not a Spark measurement: run lab 02 on your Spark for Qwen3.6.

charts.title: Single-stream decode ceiling at 273 GB/s — why the Spark playbook picks an MoE coding model
charts.caption: Arithmetic, not a benchmark: bandwidth ÷ bytes of active weights per token (sparkkit.decode_ceiling_tok_s; ~3B, 5.1B and 27B active). Real engines land below these ceilings.

charts.title: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B variants from the CLI playbook — memory to load
charts.caption: REFERENCE: sizes as the cli-coding-agent playbook's prerequisites state them. All fit in one Spark's 128 GB; the rest is KV cache for long contexts and room for other services.
